title: Furniture Workshop Automation
tagline: Orders, quotes, stock and purchasing for a made-to-order furniture workshop, automated end to end.
summary: A system for a small made-to-order furniture workshop and its showrooms. It takes orders from a form, e-mail, a calculator and a showroom tablet, prices them, watches stock and supplier prices, reorders missing materials, assigns team tasks, chases unanswered quotes and reports bestsellers weekly. It runs on n8n and Supabase (Postgres); the code was written by Claude and reviewed by a second model (Codex).

sections.title: The problem
paragraphs: The owner of a small made-to-order furniture workshop loses time on work that can be automated: orders arrive by e-mail and forms in any shape, quotes are done by eye, and a missing material is noticed only when the work has started.
This system takes the order, prices it with the same code every time, reserves materials once a human approves, reorders what is missing and keeps the customer informed.
All companies, addresses and customers in the demo data are fictional.

sections.title: What the system does
rows: Orders arrive by e-mail and form in any shape
AI turns the text into a structured order; the database prices it
Price from the supplier list + labour + margin + waste, always by the same code
A missing material shows up only during the work
Approving an order reserves materials and raises an alert on shortages immediately
Daily CSV price-list import and best_price (only prices no older than 30 days)
Customers want a price right now
Public calculator with a live quote and one-click ordering
Monday bestseller report on Slack with an AI summary
Purchase-order drafts to the cheapest supplier, approved in one click; receiving a delivery raises stock
Reminders after 3 and 7 days; after 14 days the quote is closed and a 'why not' survey is sent
Status page with a timeline, a start-of-work e-mail and a review request at the end
Inbox full of questions, complaints and spam
AI triage: orders never get lost, questions get a draft reply for approval
Showroom tablet: on-the-spot quote and a lead assigned to a showroom and salesperson

sections.title: Architecture
sections.alt: Input channels (form and e-mail, calculator, showroom tablet, status page, owner links) feed n8n workflows, which call SQL functions in Supabase. The database is the source of truth; notifications leave through email_outbox and slack_outbox queues to Gmail and Slack. A local AI model is called through a shared sub-workflow.
sections.caption: Click to enlarge. Workflows only call SQL functions and queue notifications; decisions are made by the database.

sections.title: n8n workflows
rows: Calls the local model through scripts/llm.sh (no API key)
Order from a form or e-mail → AI → validation → quote → saved
Owner approval (Basic Auth), material reservation, team task, task completion
Imports CSV price lists, low-stock report
Sends the e-mail and Slack queues
Bestsellers for 7 and 30 days + AI summary on Slack
Purchase-order drafts from materials below minimum, link approval (e-mail to supplier), delivery raises stock
Quote reminders after 3 and 7 days (AI intro, validated, fallback template), lost status after 14 days with a survey
E-mail to the customer when work starts, with a status-page link
AI classifies mail (order, question, complaint, spam); orders and uncertain cases go to intake, the rest to the owner on Slack
Google review request 7 days after completion, only when GOOGLE_REVIEW_URL is set
Showroom tablet API: quote for the customer and e-mail to the salesperson (or a lead with a note)

items.title: Logic in SQL, not in workflows
items.text: Quotes, reservations and reports are Postgres functions with tests. n8n only orchestrates, so the logic is testable without running n8n.

items.title: AI only where needed
items.text: The model reads order text and writes the report summary. Prices, stock and decisions come from code, and model output is validated; a model failure never loses an order.

items.title: A human approves
items.text: An order from e-mail does not reserve materials until the owner clicks the approval link.

items.title: Idempotency
items.text: upsert_order and calculator_order work by external_id, so a retried request never duplicates an order.

items.title: Outbox
items.text: E-mails and Slack messages are queued first with a dedup key and sent by 05-deliver. Delivery is at-least-once: a message may repeat after a crash but never disappears.

items.title: Safe defaults
items.text: E-mail delivery is off by default and, once on, goes only to an allowlist. The mock LLM must be enabled deliberately.

items.title: The database decides, not the model
items.text: The model proposes (mail category, order content, reminder intro); SQL functions decide the route, the quote and reservations. Uncertain output takes a safe path, never a silent skip.

items.title: Minimum data outside
items.text: The public API returns selling prices and totals, never material cost, labour or margin. RLS is on with no policies, so only service_role has access.
